cases.scope: Declared high-start numerical reference for continuous pitch and G release; no claim that ground-start or finite-gas keys safely complete a backflip.

limits: Received/simulated event tests and actual numerical solver traces do not replace native browser keyboard delivery or rendered video.
A signed body-axis path is not an Euler angle and is not by itself proof of a clean isolated backflip. The raw actual quaternions, contacts and axis travel are retained.

The 60 m WE1 fixture touches ground and remains a counterexample. The no-contact reference starts at 120 m with constant external supply, and loses substantial height while inverted. Neither finite-gas success nor low-altitude ground-start recovery is inferred.
The 2400-event production rolling capacity can discard the start of a long capture. Discard count and capacity remain explicit even when the wall/simulation time trace window is extended.
